THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Dubai-Style Chocolate Thin Sandwich Cookie Creami

CrumblCreamiCut Week 3, Flavor 2 — chocolate-pistachio protein Creami pint finished with a POST-SCOOP toasted-kataifi-and-pistachio-cream crunch topping. ~360 cal / 43g protein whole pint vs 810 cal for the Crumbl Dubai-Style Chocolate Thin Sandwich Cookie on the current Crumbl Davie nutrition listing.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME12 min active + 24 hr freeze + 5 min counter rest + 3 min spin + 2 min Respin + 3 min kataifi toast + 1 min pistachio-cream coat
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~360 cal | ~43g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Standard base is series infrastructure — Fairlife 2%, not fat-free. Some milk fat is intentional for texture.

Ingredients

CREAMI BASE (series standard + Dubai twist)

  • 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk
  • 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener
  • 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
  • 1/8 tsp guar gum (level measure)
  • 1 pinch salt
  • 1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder
  • 1/2 tsp pistachio emulsion (publish-corrected — see rules below)

POST-SCOOP CRUNCH TOPPING (NOT a machine mix-in)

  • 10g dry kataifi pastry strands (Greek shredded phyllo)
  • 1 tbsp pistachio cream

Allergens: dairy, tree nuts, wheat, gluten.

You want a chocolate-pistachio protein dessert with a real crunch finish that reads as a Crumbl Dubai-Style Chocolate Thin Sandwich Cookie without the 810-cal hit (per the current Crumbl Davie nutrition listing). Ep. 8 of CrumblCreamiCut, second flavor of Week 3 — follows the Mallow Sandwich Cookie Creami (W3F1). This ep introduces TWO series-firsts: (1) TOASTED KATAIFI CRUNCH TOPPING — first CCC to use real pastry crunch. Prior mix-ins were brownie chunks, graham crumb, or fruit; this is the first shatter-crunch texture in the series. Kataifi (Greek shredded phyllo pastry) is dry-toasted in an ungreased skillet, then coated in warm pistachio cream while still hot so every strand gets coated. (2) FLAVOR EMULSION IN THE BASE — first CCC using a concentrated flavor extract (pistachio emulsion) in the pre-freeze base itself. Also a PUBLISH-CORRECTED recipe — filmed with 1 tsp pistachio emulsion (too strong), publishing with 1/2 tsp as the revised recommendation. The lower dose keeps the chocolate readable and lets the kataifi topping carry the pistachio identity. 43g protein whole pint — high for the category, slightly below Mallow W3F1's 48g since there's no protein-brownie mix-in stacking on the whey base.

Method

  1. 1.POUR MILK. Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a Creami pint (or blending vessel).
  2. 2.ADD SWEETENER. 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener.
  3. 3.ADD WHEY ISOLATE. 1 serving unflavored whey isolate.
  4. 4.ADD GUAR GUM. 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy.
  5. 5.ADD SALT. 1 pinch salt.
  6. 6.ADD DUTCH COCOA. 1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder. Standard Dutch cocoa (not black cocoa — that's W3F1 Mallow's carrier). Dutch cocoa gives a milk-chocolate depth that plays well with the pistachio emulsion.
  7. 7.ADD PISTACHIO EMULSION. 1/2 tsp pistachio emulsion. PUBLISH-CORRECTED AMOUNT — the filmed batch used 1 tsp and read too strong (the pistachio drowned the chocolate). 1/2 tsp is the revised recommendation: readable chocolate base + subtle pistachio backbone that lets the kataifi topping carry the primary pistachio identity. Series-first: no prior CCC episode used a flavor emulsion in the base.
  8. 8.BLEND SMOOTH. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Base should be a uniform mauve-tinted chocolate brown (the pistachio emulsion + Dutch cocoa mix together — do not expect deep-dark chocolate here). Zero lumps, zero visible whey.
  9. 9.POUR + FREEZE (24 HR). Transfer to a Creami pint if you didn't build in the pint. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours. Do not exceed the max-fill line.
  10. 10.MEASURE KATAIFI. 10g dry kataifi pastry strands. Kataifi is shredded Greek phyllo pastry — sold refrigerated or frozen in Middle-Eastern / Greek grocery aisles as thin thread-like pastry strands. 10g is roughly a small handful; measure by weight since strand volume varies wildly.
  11. 11.DRY-TOAST KATAIFI. Add the 10g kataifi to an UNGREASED skillet over LOW heat. Stir frequently with a spatula until every strand is evenly golden and crisp. This takes 3-4 minutes. Low heat is critical — kataifi burns in under 30 seconds on medium. Series-first: no prior CCC episode used a toasted pastry crunch topping.
  12. 12.COAT WITH PISTACHIO CREAM. Turn heat off. Add 1 tbsp pistachio cream directly to the still-warm toasted kataifi in the skillet. Stir until every strand is coated in pistachio cream. Warm skillet + warm pistachio cream = even coat; the pistachio cream loosens against the toasted strands and coats them without clumping. Set the coated kataifi mixture aside — it will crisp back up as it cools slightly.
  13. 13.REST 5 MIN + FIRST SPIN. Pull the frozen Creami pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. The first spin may look grainy; expected because the no-liquid Respin finishes the texture.
  14. 14.NO-LIQUID RESPIN. Run one Respin cycle with NO added liquid. No milk, no water — the base has enough moisture on its own. This is a texture-finish pass, not a mix-in incorporation pass (the topping stays out of the machine). Same cycle family as W1F1-W3F1, but this is the first ep where Respin is a texture-only pass (no mix-in going in).
  15. 15.SCOOP. Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Smooth chocolate-pistachio Creami with a mauve-brown tint. Ready for the topping.
  16. 16.ADD PISTACHIO-KATAIFI TOPPING. Pile ALL of the pistachio-cream-coated toasted kataifi over the scoops. The topping is a POST-SCOOP GARNISH — NOT a machine mix-in. Adding kataifi to the pint before Respin would (a) crush the crunch into paste and (b) turn the Creami gummy from the pistachio cream. Keeping it as a post-scoop finish preserves the shatter-crunch texture and the pistachio-cream coat identity. Serve immediately.
  17. 17.SERVE. Deep chocolate-pistachio Creami finished with a generous crown of toasted-kataifi-and-pistachio-cream crunch. Eat within 2-3 minutes of topping — kataifi softens fast against the cold Creami surface if it sits.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Level 1/8 tsp guar gum. Heaped = gummy.
  • 1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa (not black cocoa — that's W3F1 Mallow's carrier). Dutch cocoa reads as milk-chocolate depth here, which is intentional.

If something fails

Base tastes pistachio-dominant / can't taste the chocolate: You used 1 tsp of pistachio emulsion (the filmed amount) instead of 1/2 tsp. Emulsions are concentrated — 1/2 tsp is the revised recommendation and gives a warm pistachio backbone under a readable chocolate base. If already blended, add another 1 tbsp Dutch cocoa to rebalance and re-blend before freezing, OR accept it as a pistachio-forward variant.

Base tastes muted / chocolate is barely there: Check the Dutch cocoa — 1 tbsp is the target. Verify the powder wasn't clumped in the pint. Also verify pistachio emulsion is 1/2 tsp (not less) — a trace of emulsion carries the pistachio identity that the topping builds on.

Kataifi burned or scorched: Skillet was too hot. Kataifi is thin phyllo — it toasts in 3-4 minutes on LOW heat and burns in <30 seconds on medium. Reduce heat, stir constantly. If already burned, start over with fresh kataifi; scorched pastry ruins the whole topping.

Kataifi soft and floppy, not crunchy: Under-toasted. Return to LOW heat and continue stirring until every strand is evenly golden and crisp (not just tan). The strands should feel brittle when squeezed between fingers. Under-toasted kataifi turns to mush against the cold Creami.

Pistachio cream clumped instead of coating the kataifi: Skillet cooled too much before the pistachio cream went in. Reheat the skillet to just-warm (turn on low for 30 seconds) and stir again. Alternative: microwave the pistachio cream 5-10 seconds until soft before stirring in. Aim for a loose, drape-able coat on every strand.

Grainy or powdery after Regular Ice Cream (first spin): Expected on this flavor. Run one no-liquid Respin — it finishes the texture without any mix-in. Don't skip Respin because 'the first spin looked fine.'

Icy after Respin: You added milk or water during Respin. The base has enough moisture — no-liquid Respin is a series-wide rule for texture-only passes. Verify Fairlife 2% (not fat-free), verify LEVEL 1/8 tsp guar gum, verify the full 24-hour freeze happened upright and level.

Whole pint turned gummy or stringy: Kataifi or pistachio cream was added to the pint before or during Respin. Both are POST-SCOOP garnishes only — never in the pint. Reprocess a new pint from the base if this happens; there's no rescue for a topping-Respun pint.

Base color is mauve-brown, not deep-dark chocolate: Expected. Dutch cocoa + pistachio emulsion together read as milk-chocolate with a mauve tint, not deep-dark chocolate. If you want a darker base, sub 1 tbsp Dutch cocoa for 1 tbsp black cocoa (Dutch-processed extra-dark — see W3F1 Mallow ep for context). Note that black cocoa shifts the ep away from the milk-chocolate/pistachio Crumbl identity toward an OREO-adjacent profile.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store the frozen pint upright and level in the freezer for up to 1 week pre-spin. Store the pistachio-kataifi topping mixture separately in an airtight container at room temperature (24 hours max — the pistachio-cream coat keeps the kataifi from softening for that long; longer sits soften the crunch).

Reheat: N/A — serve immediately after Respin + topping. If leftovers must refreeze, skip the pistachio-kataifi on the second pass (that batch is done), level the surface first, and reprocess only when the frozen top is flat. Toast fresh kataifi on any repeat serving.

Lasts: Frozen pint (pre-spin) keeps 1 week. Pistachio-kataifi topping keeps 24 hours in an airtight container at room temp. Assembled Creami keeps its texture for 2-3 minutes before the kataifi softens against the cold surface — eat immediately.

Estimated nutrition

~360 cal | ~43g protein.

~360 cal / 43g protein per whole finished pint (single serving). Component breakdown: 1 cup Fairlife 2% (~120 cal / 13g protein) + 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~110 cal / 25g protein — varies by brand) + 2 tbsp monk fruit sweetener (~0 cal) + 1/8 tsp guar gum (~trace) + 1 tbsp Dutch cocoa (~15 cal / 1g protein) + 1/2 tsp pistachio emulsion (~5 cal / 0g protein — publish-corrected from 1 tsp filmed) + 10g kataifi (~35 cal / 1g protein) + 1 tbsp pistachio cream (~75 cal / 2g protein — varies wildly by brand, some are 40 cal/tbsp, some are 100+) = ~360 cal / 42g protein raw sum. Rounds to the creator-provided ~360 / 43 target. Marked estimated. Verify exact Fairlife / whey isolate / Dutch cocoa / pistachio emulsion / kataifi / pistachio cream labels before publishing as label-verified. Compared to the 810-cal Crumbl Dubai-Style Chocolate Thin Sandwich Cookie listed on the current Crumbl Davie nutrition page — the Creami version delivers similar flavor identity at ~44% of the Crumbl calorie count with roughly 20× the protein per serving. Not sponsored, not endorsed, not affiliated with Crumbl, LorAnn, Ninja, Fairlife, or any kataifi / pistachio-cream brand. Allergens: dairy (milk + whey isolate), tree nuts (pistachio cream + pistachio emulsion), wheat/gluten (kataifi). Soy + egg NOT verified — check whey / pistachio cream / emulsion / kataifi labels before claiming free-of.

Flavor target

First spoon: chocolate + warm pistachio note across the whole pint. Bite: toasted kataifi shatter-crunch coated in pistachio cream lands as the Dubai-cookie identity moment. Chocolate reads as milk-chocolate depth, not super-dark. Pistachio should register as a warm-nutty backbone in the base + a bright pistachio hit in the topping. Whole pint should taste like the Crumbl Dubai-Style cookie deconstructed into ice cream: chocolate cookie backbone + pistachio cream + kataifi crunch, one bowl.

Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Full recipe as written — whole pint = 1 adult serving at ~360 cal / 43g protein. Second flavor of the CrumblCreamiCut Week 3 lineup.

Kid plate

Kid

Same base works as a smaller portion. Kids typically split a pint 2-3 ways vs the whole-pint-per-adult default. If the kid isn't into pistachio, keep the base (chocolate reads fine on its own at 1/2 tsp emulsion) but swap the kataifi topping for plain protein-brownie crumb or crushed graham. Serve the crunch topping in a separate bowl for kids who like to sprinkle-and-mix themselves.

Brands I use

Fairlife
2% Ultra-Filtered Milk
Series-standard base — same 1 cup + 1 serving whey isolate foundation as W1F1 through W3F1. Not sponsored.
Dutch-process cocoa (any brand)
1 tbsp per pint — standard Dutch-process cocoa powder
Milk-chocolate depth in the base. Common brands: Droste, Guittard, Rodelle, King Arthur. NOT the same as black cocoa (which is W3F1 Mallow's carrier). Not sponsored.
Pistachio emulsion (LorAnn or similar)
1/2 tsp per pint — concentrated pistachio flavor extract
Series-first: first CCC ep using a flavor emulsion in the base. LorAnn is the most common food-grade pistachio emulsion; OliveNation and Amoretti also sell food-grade versions. 1/2 tsp is the PUBLISH-CORRECTED amount — filmed with 1 tsp, revised down after taste-test. Concentrated: more is not better. Not sponsored.
Kataifi
10g dry pastry strands (Greek shredded phyllo)
Series-first crunch topping. Kataifi is refrigerated or frozen in Middle-Eastern / Greek grocery aisles. Any brand works — measure by weight (10g), not strand count. Dry-toast over LOW heat in an ungreased skillet. Not sponsored.
Pistachio cream (any brand)
1 tbsp per pint — sweetened pourable pistachio spread
Coats the toasted kataifi and delivers the primary pistachio identity in the topping. Common brands: Fiddyment Farms, Terra Kitchens, Trader Joe's. Do NOT confuse with pistachio butter (thicker, unsweetened). Not sponsored.
Unflavored Whey Isolate
Any clean-tasting unflavored whey isolate — ~28g protein per serving
Series-standard protein spine. Isolate (not concentrate) blends smoother.
Ninja Creami
Ninja Creami machine (any current model)
The full CrumblCreamiCut series relies on the Ninja Creami's Regular Ice Cream + Respin cycles. Not sponsored.
